title: Degree of the pullback under a finite morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite surjective morphism of proper
varieties over a field $k$, let $\mathcal M$ be an
ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module,
and let $\deg(f)=[k(X):k(Y)]$ be the degree of the finite
dominant morphism $f$
(function fields). Then

$$
\deg_{f^*\mathcal M}(X)=\deg(f)\deg_{\mathcal M}(Y),
$$

where the degrees are those of [def-sc-hilbert-degree].

proof.text: First, deg_{f^*\mathcal M}(X) is well-defined: f is finite and hence affine, so its pullback of the ample invertible module \mathcal M is ample by [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] (Stacks Morphisms, Tag 0892). Since f is affine and f^*\mathcal M^{\otimes m} is quasi-coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] (Stacks Cohomology, Tag 089W) gives \chi(X,f^*\mathcal M^{\otimes m})=\chi(Y,f_*f^*\mathcal M^{\otimes m}). By the projection formula, \chi(Y,f_*f^*\mathcal M^{\otimes m})=\chi(Y,f_*\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes m}).

Since f is finite, f_*\mathcal O_X is a quasi-coherent \mathcal O_Y-module of finite type [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; Y is of finite type over k, hence noetherian, so f_*\mathcal O_X is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] (Stacks Tag 01XZ). Choose an affine neighbourhood V=Spec(A) of the generic point of integral Y. The module M=\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal O_X) is finite over the noetherian ring A, hence finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]. Its localization at the generic prime is the finite field extension k(X) over k(Y), hence is free of rank r=[k(X):k(Y)]=\deg(f). Applying [lem-sc-finitely-presented-free-at-prime-principal] at that prime gives a nonempty principal open on which f_*\mathcal O_X is free of rank r; thus it is free of rank r on a nonempty open of Y. Apply [lem-sc-generic-rank-leading-degree]. Since dim X=dim Y by [lem-sc-finite-surjective-dimension], the m^g coefficient, and hence g! times that coefficient in [def-sc-hilbert-degree], is multiplied by r. Therefore \deg_{f^*\mathcal M}(X)=\deg(f)\deg_{\mathcal M}(Y).
